Preparing your data

Source: vignettes/articles/preparing-data.Rmd
preparing-data.Rmd

The analyses of the package take the same objects: a community matrix, a tree, a table of predictors and, for some of them, coordinates and areas. This article goes from tables like those of a field survey to a first test. The data below are simulated, to keep the article self-contained.

library(comdynamite)

set.seed(1)
tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(10)
tree$tip.label <- paste0("Genus_species", 1:10)
sites <- expand.grid(x = 1:8, y = 1:5)
sites$site <- paste0("s", seq_len(nrow(sites)))
sites$depth <- sites$x * 10 + rnorm(nrow(sites), sd = 5)
sites$habitat <- rep(c("forest", "open"), length.out = nrow(sites))
traits <- species_traits(tree, lambda = 1, optima_range = c(0, 90), rmax_range = c(0, 30))
wide <- simulate_static(traits, sites$depth, incidence = TRUE)$abundance
records <- data.frame(site = sites$site[row(wide)[wide > 0]],
                      species = sub("_", " ", tree$tip.label[col(wide)[wide > 0]]))
head(records)
#>   site        species
#> 1   s3 Genus species1
#> 2   s4 Genus species1
#> 3   s5 Genus species1
#> 4   s6 Genus species1
#> 5   s7 Genus species1
#> 6   s8 Genus species1

The community matrix

comm has one row per site and one column per species, with numbers only, so names of sites go to the row names. A table of records becomes a matrix with table().

comm <- records |>
  with(table(site, species)) |>
  unclass()
comm[1:3, 1:3]
#>      species
#> site  Genus species1 Genus species10 Genus species2
#>   s1               0               0              1
#>   s10              0               0              1
#>   s11              1               0              1

A site without records does not appear in this matrix. pcc_test(), pcps_test(), phylo_beta_test() and phylo_beta() need at least one individual in every site, so sites without any species stay out of those analyses.

The tree

Species are matched to the tips by name, in any order. The most frequent problem is the spelling of names, as here, where the table has spaces and the tree has underscores.

setdiff(colnames(comm), tree$tip.label)[1:3]
#> [1] "Genus species1"  "Genus species10" "Genus species2"
colnames(comm) <- gsub(" ", "_", colnames(comm))
setdiff(colnames(comm), tree$tip.label)
#> character(0)

Species in only one of the two are dropped with a warning that names them, so read these warnings before reading results. Analyses that use distances among species need branch lengths, whereas node_contrasts() also works with a topology.

Predictors

env has one row per site and numeric columns. Factors become dummy variables with model.matrix(), without the intercept column. Missing values are not accepted, so sites without data need to leave comm and env together.

rownames(sites) <- sites$site
sites <- sites[rownames(comm), ]
env <- cbind(depth = sites$depth, open = model.matrix(~ habitat, sites)[, "habitatopen"])
rownames(env) <- rownames(comm)
head(env, 3)
#>        depth open
#> s1  14.10611    0
#> s10 12.64624    1
#> s11 27.60925    0

When comm and the other tables all have row names, sites are matched by name. Otherwise they are matched by position, and the rows need to be in the same order.

Areas and coordinates

For historical hypotheses, biogeography_matrix() builds the events of node_test() from the area of each site, with NA for sites outside all areas. Polygons give the area with sf::st_join(). Events should come from a hypothesis stated in advance.

area <- ifelse(sites$x <= 3, "west", ifelse(sites$x >= 6, "east", NA))
names(area) <- rownames(comm)
events <- biogeography_matrix(area, list(barrier = list("west", "east")))
table(events)
#> events
#> -1  0  1 
#> 15 10 15

Sites of an area are usually neighbours, and free permutations then reject too often. patch_permutations() gives a null model for landscapes with edges, and rigid_permutations() another that keeps the distance between the sides of an event, for sides with room to move (see the article on analysing clades). Coordinates should be projected, because distances are Euclidean; sf::st_transform() does this.

coords <- as.matrix(sites[, c("x", "y")])
area_moves <- patch_permutations(coords, events, n_perm = 99)

A first test 

nodes <- node_contrasts(tree)
out <- node_test(comm, nodes, env, events, n_perm = 99, area_permutations = area_moves)
out
#> <mc_node_test> 9 nodes, 9 tested
#> permutations: 99 free of sites, 99 of species, of areas barrier 99; smallest possible p: 0.01
#> nodes with p (max) <= 0.05: 0 before correction, 0 after

The number of permutations here keeps the article fast. Use more than this in an analysis, because the smallest possible p-value depends on it and it is printed with the results.

What each analysis needs

Function comm Tree Predictors Other
node_test() sites by species contrasts from node_contrasts() env biogeography, optional
pcc_test() no empty sites with branch lengths env
pcps_test() no empty sites with branch lengths env
phylo_beta_test() no empty sites with branch lengths env
phylo_vector() sites by species with branch lengths one predictor
trait_partition() sites by species traits or phylo_vector() scores env space
